passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: CORPORATE DEVELOPMENTS Introduction We are a diversified holding company with natural gas and electric utility operations (serving customers in Wisconsin, Illinois, Michigan, and Minnesota), an approximately 60% equity ownership interest in ATC (a for-profit electric transmission company regulated by the FERC and certain state regulatory commissions), and non-utility energy infrastructure operations through We Power (which owns generation assets in Wisconsin that it leases to WE), Bluewater (which owns underground natural gas storage facilities in Michigan), and WECI (which holds ownership interests in several renewable generating facilities). Corporate Strategy We are working to build and sustain long-term value for our shareholders and customers by supporting economic growth in our region while focusing on the fundamentals of our business: reliability, operating efficiency, financial discipline, environmental stewardship, exceptional customer care, and safety. Our capital plan provides a roadmap for us to achieve this goal. It is a plan premised upon maintaining superior reliability, delivering savings for customers, and growing our investment in the future of energy. Throughout our strategic planning process, we take into account important developments, risks and opportunities, including new technologies, customer preferences and affordability, energy resiliency efforts, and sustainability. Supporting Economic Growth Within Our Communities Economic growth continues in our Wisconsin service territories. Companies are investing in major projects, including data centers and modern manufacturing facilities. We anticipate electric demand growth in the years ahead from these economic developments. Microsoft has announced plans to invest over $20 billion in data centers in southern Wisconsin over the next several years, and we expect up to 2.6 GWs of load growth in the Milwaukee-to-Chicago corridor through 2030. Additionally, Vantage Data Centers plans to develop a large data center campus in Port Washington that is forecasted to add 1.3 GWs of demand through 2030. This site has the potential to add an incremental 2.2 GWs, for a total of up to 3.5 GWs over time. We are working closely with these large customers to provide power to meet this substantial projected demand. In 2025, we submitted a proposal to the PSCW for new VLC and Bespoke Resources tariffs. The proposed tariffs specifically address the unique needs of VLCs while protecting our other customers and shareholders. See Note 26, Regulatory Environment, for more information on the VLC and Bespoke Resources tariffs. To meet the forecasted electric demand growth in the years ahead, greater capacity will be required to provide affordable, reliable, and clean energy for our communities. Our capital plan addresses that demand with a range of planned investments in natural gas-fired generation, renewables, and battery storage. We plan on investing approximately $5.4 billion from 2026 to 2030 in a combination of efficient natural gas-fired generation, including: • 3,300 MWs of CTs (we plan on constructing a new natural gas lateral pipeline to support the CTs planned at our OCPP site); and • 18

passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: We are subject to a variety of risks, many of which are beyond our control, that may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. You should carefully consider the following risk factors, as well as the other information included in this report and other documents filed by us with the SEC from time to time, when making an investment decision. Risks Related to Legislation and Regulation Our business is significantly impacted by governmental legislation, regulation, and oversight. We are subject to significant state, local, and federal governmental legislation and regulations, including regulations by the various utility commissions in the states where we serve customers. Legislation and regulation significantly influence our operating environment, may affect our ability to recover costs from utility customers, affect our ability to implement our corporate strategy, and cause us to incur substantial compliance and other costs. Changes in legislation or regulations, their interpretation, or the imposition of new legislation or regulations could also significantly impact our business operations. Many aspects of our operations are impacted by government legislation and regulations, including, but not limited to: the rates we charge our retail electric, natural gas, and steam customers; the authorized rates of return of our utilities; construction and operation of electric generating facilities and electric and natural gas distribution systems, including the ability to recover such costs; decommissioning generating facilities, the ability to recover the related costs, and continuing to recover the return on the net book value of these facilities; wholesale power service practices; electric reliability requirements; participation in the interstate natural gas pipeline capacity market; standards of service; issuance of securities; short-term debt obligations; transactions with affiliates; and billing practices. Failure to comply with any applicable rules or regulations may lead to customer refunds, penalties, and other payments, which could materially and adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition. The rates, including adjustments determined under riders, we are allowed to charge our customers for retail and wholesale services have the most significant impact on our financial condition, results of operations, and liquidity. Rate regulation provides us an opportunity to recover prudently incurred costs and earn a reasonable rate of return on invested capital. However, our ability to obtain rate adjustments in the future is dependent upon regulatory action, the outcome of which can be influenced by the level of opposition by intervening parties; potential rate impacts; increasing levels of regulatory review; and changes in the political, regulatory, or legislative environments. There is no assurance that our regulators will consider all of our costs to have been prudently incurred. In addition, our rate proceedings may not always result in rates that fully recover our costs or provide for a reasonable ROE. credit_strengths.text: WEC Energy Group's regulated utility footprint across Wisconsin, Illinois, Michigan and Minnesota, plus its transmission affiliate, delivers stable and predictable cash flows. Operating cash flow has grown steadily over the past three years, reflecting constructive rate outcomes and a diversified asset base. This recurring cash generation underpins the investment-grade profile and supports the heavy capital program without reliance on volatile merchant revenues.

Operating margins remain solid at roughly twenty-three percent, only modestly below the utility sector median, while operating income has risen each year. The company's scale and regulated returns provide a buffer against cost inflation. Interest coverage of about two and a half times is broadly in line with peers, indicating that earnings comfortably cover the current interest burden despite the elevated debt load.

key_risks.text: The risk-factor passage highlights that rate regulation significantly influences financial condition, and there is no assurance regulators will deem all costs prudently incurred or allow full recovery. Adverse rate proceedings could pressure cash flow precisely when the capital plan requires substantial funding. This regulatory dependency is a core credit risk for WEC's utility subsidiaries and their ability to service debt.

Debt maturities are sizable, with a meaningful portion due within the next twelve months and a further tranche in year two. The company must refinance these obligations amid a rising rate environment, and its short-term borrowings add refinancing risk. The debt note confirms the layered maturity profile, which requires continuous access to capital markets to avoid liquidity strain.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Net leverage stands at approximately five point nine times, above the utility sector median, and the indicative financial risk profile is highly leveraged. Operating cash flow covers only about fifteen percent of debt, below the sector median, indicating limited headroom. The company's debt-servicing capacity relies on stable regulated cash flows and continued access to refinancing, leaving little cushion for operational setbacks.

Interest coverage of roughly two and a half times is adequate but not strong, and the current ratio is below one, reflecting a working capital deficit typical of utilities but still a liquidity consideration. Cash on hand is minimal relative to debt, so servicing depends on ongoing operating cash flow and refinancing. A decline in cash generation could quickly erode coverage.

overall_credit_view.text: WEC Energy Group presents a highly leveraged utility credit with stable regulated cash flows but limited financial cushion. Leverage sits above the sector median and the indicative risk profile is highly leveraged, while cash flow to debt is below peers. The company's credit quality hinges on supportive regulation and continued capital market access to refinance maturing debt and fund its large capital plan.

Our forward-looking view is that credit metrics will remain under pressure as the capital program expands, with shareholder dividends absorbing a significant portion of operating cash flow. The absence of capex data prevents a precise free cash flow assessment, but the disclosed capital plan implies ongoing external funding needs. We would monitor regulatory outcomes and refinancing conditions closely.

credit_strengths.text: WEC Energy Group 受監管公用事業業務遍及威斯康辛州、伊利諾州、密西根州及明尼蘇達州，加上其輸電聯營公司，帶來穩定且可預測的現金流。過去三年營運現金流穩步增長，反映有利的費率結果及多元化的資產基礎。此經常性現金產生能力支撐投資級別狀況，並支持龐大的資本計劃，而無需依賴波動的商業性收入。
營運利潤率維持穩健，約為百分之二十三，僅略低於公用事業行業中位數，而營運收入逐年上升。公司的規模及受監管回報為成本通脹提供緩衝。利息覆蓋率約為兩倍半，與同業大致一致，顯示盈利足以舒適地覆蓋當前利息負擔，儘管債務負擔偏高。

key_risks.text: 風險因素段落強調，費率監管顯著影響財務狀況，且無法保證監管機構會認為所有成本均屬審慎發生或允許全額回收。不利的費率程序可能在資本計劃需要大量資金之際對現金流構成壓力。此監管依賴性是 WEC 公用事業子公司及其償債能力的核心信用風險。
債務到期規模龐大，其中相當部分將於未來十二個月內到期，第二年另有另一批到期。公司必須在利率上升的環境中為這些債務再融資，而其短期借款增加再融資風險。債務附註確認了分層到期結構，需要持續進入資本市場以避免流動性壓力。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 淨槓桿約為五點九倍，高於公用事業行業中位數，而指示性財務風險狀況為高度槓桿。營運現金流僅覆蓋約百分之十五的債務，低於行業中位數，顯示緩衝空間有限。公司的償債能力依賴穩定的受監管現金流及持續的再融資渠道，對營運挫折的緩衝甚少。
利息覆蓋率約為兩倍半，屬足夠但不強勁，而流動比率低於一，反映公用事業典型的營運資金赤字，但仍是一項流動性考量。手頭現金相對債務極少，因此償債依賴持續的營運現金流及再融資。現金產生能力下降可能迅速侵蝕覆蓋率。

overall_credit_view.text: WEC Energy Group 呈現高度槓桿的公用事業信用，受監管現金流穩定但財務緩衝有限。槓桿高於行業中位數，指示性風險狀況為高度槓桿，而現金流對債務比率低於同業。公司的信用質素取決於支持性監管及持續進入資本市場，以再融資到期債務並為其龐大資本計劃提供資金。
我們的前瞻性觀點是，隨著資本計劃擴大，信用指標將持續受壓，股東股息吸收營運現金流的顯著部分。缺乏資本開支數據使我們無法精確評估自由現金流，但披露的資本計劃意味著持續的外部融資需求。我們將密切監察監管結果及再融資狀況。
